web-search.description: Query the public web and scholarly indexes (e.g. Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, arXiv, ORCID, OpenAlex) and read the resulting pages.
web-search.contract: The runtime must give the agent a way to issue search queries and retrieve result content, and every result the agent cites must carry a resolvable URL or DOI.
web-search.whenUnavailable: Do NOT claim to have searched; state explicitly that web search was unavailable and rely only on existing context and your training knowledge. Do not fabricate URLs or DOIs.

code-execution.description: Run short, self-contained scripts in a sandboxed interpreter with common numeric libraries available. The sandbox adds nothing of its own: standard output contains exactly what the script prints, in exactly the structure the script prints it — so print the values a checker needs as one clearly structured final line, and quote that output verbatim wherever evidence asks for a result. A failed run comes back to you, the submitter, as a bug report: debug it from the returned stderr/stdout, fix your script, and rerun — reruns are safe.
code-execution.contract: The runtime must execute a supplied script in isolation and return its stdout/stderr and exit status to the agent, unaltered. No network or session-state access from inside the sandbox. Failures are returned to the submitting agent to debug — the runtime never edits or retries the script on the agent's behalf.
code-execution.whenUnavailable: Do NOT claim to have run code; include the full script source in your output so a human can verify it manually. State explicitly that code execution was unavailable.

gpu-execution.description: Run a minimal, self-contained bash script body through the deployment owner's approved GPU profile after that profile passes a GPU probe. The profile supplies the scheduler, resources, environment setup and runtime ceiling; the agent supplies only the computation. Use a GPU only for a check that needs accelerator hardware, with one experiment per claim and at most two submissions per task unless the user explicitly requests more; host limits still apply. Print the inputs, method and result needed to check the claim. The response contains the job's state and diagnostic output, with any truncation identified; generated files may be listed without their contents. A queue, scheduler, allocation or environment failure is not scientific evidence.
gpu-execution.contract: The runtime must expose gpu.run only through a server profile approved by the deployment owner and verified by a successful GPU probe. Profile changes invalidate that verification. It must insert the agent's script body unchanged into that profile, enforce the deployment's resource and time limits, and return the actual scheduler state and stdout/stderr without interpreting them as research findings or concealing truncation. The agent must not add scheduler directives, submit nested jobs or alter the approved setup. Package installation is allowed only when the approved profile explicitly supports it. A failed computation returns diagnostics to its author, who may make one correction within the two-submission task budget; scheduler, queue or environment failures must be reported without blind resubmission. The runtime never edits or retries the computation on the agent's behalf.
gpu-execution.whenUnavailable: Do NOT claim to have run anything on a GPU or bypass the GPU tool through another execution capability. The deployment owner must review the GPU profile and approve its probe; that probe must succeed before GPU execution becomes available. Continue tasks that do not need a GPU. If a conclusion needs an unperformed GPU experiment, mark it unverified and provide the exact proposed script and expected check in the output where relevant; never interpret missing GPU access as evidence against the scientific claim.

attachment-access.description: Read and search the content of files attached to the submission under review: list the inventory, read one file, or search every text attachment for a word, phrase, or regular expression in a single deterministic call (matching lines with file path and line number).
attachment-access.contract: The runtime must resolve each attachment named in the agent's input to its full content (or a faithful text rendition) on request, and must answer inventory and search requests deterministically host-side — never by making the agent read files one by one to locate something.
attachment-access.whenUnavailable: Do NOT claim to have read or searched attachments; state explicitly that attachment access was unavailable and reason only from the metadata and descriptions provided in your input.

taxonomy-access.description: Read the LIVE shared scientific taxonomy (domain > field > subfield > topic) maintained by the Brain Registry: fetch the complete latest tree as a names-only outline, and resolve a field name to its exact position.
taxonomy-access.contract: The runtime must answer every read from the single shared taxonomy store at its latest committed revision — reflecting every user's accepted edits, not a run-local copy — and stamp every answer with that revision. Reads only: recording placement decisions is a deterministic runtime step, never an agent tool.
taxonomy-access.whenUnavailable: Do NOT invent taxonomy positions or parents; state explicitly that the shared taxonomy was unavailable and mark every member you were asked to place as undecidable instead of guessing.

notes-access.description: Search the thinker's working notes: the complete recorded thinking behind the chain under review (the seat's first pass and every repair since), kept out of the prompt and reached through one search tool with several modes — find words or phrases and return the sentence, paragraph or a window around each hit; list the thinker's hedges and open checks, the alternatives it weighed, and its assumptions, cited sources, calculations and conclusions; browse an outline and read paragraphs by id. Scoped per task to the seat under review and to the chain position already shown.
notes-access.contract: The runtime must hold every chain-writing task's recorded thinking in full (never truncated) and answer each review task's searches deterministically host-side over exactly one seat's notes, hiding thinking recorded after the chain position that task has been shown. The notes never enter a prompt; the agent reads them only through the tool. Reads only, and confidential to the board: the thinker is never told its notes are read.
notes-access.whenUnavailable: Do NOT claim to have read the thinker's notes; review the chain text on its own and your own verified evidence, and state that the notes were unavailable only if asked.

fact-table.description: Consult the supreme judge through fact_table about independently asserted substantive claims, cited badges, or their use in a report. The tool is a conversational channel: lookup asks the judge to find conceptually related facts, status asks about current badges and why they were issued, submit presents a claim and evidence for independent verification, and approve asks whether a specific badge supports a specific report under its conditions. An optional message can ask a follow-up scientific question. Only supreme-judge tasks receive raw table entries; other agents receive its explanations, actual F:n badges and badgeHash revision fingerprints, and approval receipts where applicable. Original proofs and calculations and verified sources are valid evidence routes. Supported direct reasoning needs no separate badge; there is no badge minimum or blanket common-knowledge, derivation, or assumption exemption.
fact-table.contract: The runtime keeps one durable scoped fact record per run. For this mediated control, every agent-facing mode calls the supreme judge; no raw entries or deterministic lookup/status results are exposed to other agents. The judge semantically examines all entries in the permitted scope in batches, without a lexical candidate gate, and compares claims, implications, conditions, and conflicts. Independent critics retain a frozen shared snapshot plus their own private findings; mediation must never disclose peer private facts or requester identities. The verification role checks new claims with its own capabilities and re-examines conflicting evidence. Only the host commits rulings and generates badgeHash fingerprints and report/version-bound approval receipts. Approval of semantic support must be backed by a real current record and persisted receipt; models cannot create hashes, IDs, or permissions. Supreme-judge tasks receive raw scoped entries directly and never recursively consult themselves.
fact-table.whenUnavailable: Do NOT invent justification badges or cite nonexistent [F:n] ids. State the support you actually checked and distinguish established claims from unresolved ones. Directly inspectable reasoning can still be assessed, but lack of verification for a substantive independent claim must remain visible. An explicit assumption scopes a conditional argument; it does not establish the premise or license an unconditional conclusion.
